content.comment_body: I'm trying to set up an MQTT connection from my [company_name] [product_name] using [product_name] [version_no] to a Zoho IoT device, with proper credentials (username, password, TLS setup). However, I keep getting a 'Failed to parse' error when connecting to Zoho’s MQTT broker. When I use a local Mosquitto MQTT broker instead, the connection is successful, confirming that my MQTT setup on the device is correct. Given this, I’m unsure why the connection is blocked when targeting Zoho’s broker. Could it be due to: • MQTT protocol version incompatibility? • TLS handshake or CA certificate mismatch? • Differences in authentication methods? • Issues with DNS or hostname resolution on [product_name]? • Or, do I need to use something like Node-RED as an MQTT bridge between the device and Zoho? Any advice on troubleshooting or potential workarounds is appreciated.
This topic has been closed because the question was posted twice. Please refer to the active thread here: [document]. Kind regards, [user_name]

While the connection to a local Mosquitto broker works, attempts to connect to Zoho’s broker result in a 'Failed to parse' error, indicating possible protocol, certificate, or authentication issues. This highlights challenges with interoperability between [company_name] devices and third-party cloud platforms.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the [company_name] [product_name] and [product_name] [version_no] to establish a secure, reliable MQTT connection with the Zoho IoT broker using standard credentials and settings, similar to the successful connection with Mosquitto.
